game_name: Orwell: Keeping an Eye On You
review_text_raw:
Orwell is an intriguing game that does not let you get away with bad jokes. The player will have to use rationality and puzzle together the real story from reading other people's perspectives on the same events, and one must be careful what information is handed over to Big Brother.

The game lets you choose whether you want to let people get away with things or if you hand every piece of information to your superior, and it's easy to let yourself be brainwashed and forget that one surveills real people and not just stains in the system, which the game is really good at making you believe. In addition to this, the game had good sound effects which kept you on the edge of your seat, as well as having many plot-twists and unexpected elements to it. 
Not to mention the witty references to the novel 1984 by George Orwell, which effectively added an element of familiarity to those who are acquainted with the novel.

I recommend this game to both people who know 1984 and to those who don't (and possibly want to), as this is a good introduction to the novel and it gives you an interesting perspective in how it feels to work for Big Brother. Therefore, I give this game a rating of 10/10.

game_name: Orwell: Keeping an Eye On You
review_text_raw:
My first contact with Orwell was back in 2017 when there was some event in my local town square where there were couple of PCs with few games on it for everyone interested to play, and Orwell was one of them. This game actually taught me very very advanced English and I shall ever be so grateful for it.

This game is based on George Orwell's novel "1984" where he mentions the phrase "Big Brother" for the first time. I've never read it but after playing both games [yes there is a second one] I think I just might. Basically it means that you're being spied on all the time. I could describe and explain what "ORWELL" really stands for but that would be a huge spoiler and nobody wants that, right? It is very political, but if I got to play it, a person who knows jack crap about politics, everyone can play it.
If you've never played it before, the average play time is around 4-5 hours, but once you get to do more playthroughs in it can be done in little over 2 hours. I also really liked the low-poly design of the pictures, it really adds to the overall graphics experience.

What was a bad move in my opinion was the fact that you're not actually doing any research on your own, the game automatically highlights the important "datachunks" for you to upload to a corresponding profile. But on the other hand I can imagine how difficult it would have to be for the developers to implement this function. If everyone would put there even just slightly different things it would be a mess. But it's a nice thought to think about.

If you're interested in politics or simply want to improve your English, play this game. I'm pretty sure you will have to translate every third word or so because like I said, it is very professionally written but that's the beauty of it.

game_name: Orwell: Keeping an Eye On You
review_text_raw:
I have been playing video games since the Atari 2600 and out of the many games I have played only 5  have inspired me to award them my own personal score of 10. Orwell has joined this very exclusive list for me. The game is a masterclass of using the medium of video games to make poignant social commentary that feels gripping and authentic. 

Daniel Marx (Game Designer) is a fantastic writer who gives each one of his characters a very distinct voice using colloquial dialogue and expressions that stay consistent for each character throughout the course of the 5 chapters of the story. His ability to create believable characters with personalities and motivations that feel real is the key to making the message of the game resonate. This isn't a simple story of noble heroes and evil villains, this is an examination of complex people and their struggles to reconcile their beliefs and their feelings, their fears and their ability to summon up the courage to do what they feel is right. 

The Gameplay is simple to understand, but choices made by the player do have branching consequences. Reminiscent of Telltale games and other members of the narrrative genre with a choice driven structure. The game manages to give the player a sense of real agency in the outcomes of the story, and have genuinley significant differences at several key moments. My mind spins at the challenge of writing a story that is able to stay consistent throughout its length, and yet offer a significant number of alternatives that need to be followed to their logical conclusion. Again, my compliments to Daniel Marx on his writing skills and game design. Impressive. Very impressive. 

The art style reminded me of the polygonal look of games like Out of This World and Flashback from the early and mid 90's with improved technology that looks good and yet remains accessible to all players even ones with 8 year old laptops (such as myself). Compliments to Melanie Taylor for an aesthetic that is easy on the eye and hardware. 

In the end, the writing, gameplay and art all serve to execute on making a statement about the ever increasing surveillance that is taking place in our own world and it is no suprise that the invasion of privacy that is possible at this very moment is something that can chill to the bone. We are at a crossroads in the story of humanity, whether the next chapters are dominated by the decision to sacrifice freedom for security or the acceptance that freedom carries risks, but is far better than a world where everyone is always suspect of being an enemy of the state and a target for elimination. 

Provided you do not object to reading a great deal (as there is no voice acting), this game will provide you with 10 hours of riveting narrative that will undoubtedly leave you questioning how much autonomy we are willing to surrender for the illusion of safety that a large surveillance state seemingly affords. 

I cannot recommend this game highly enough.

P.S. Additionally many thanks to Michael Kluge (Programming) for his coding work. The game runs very well. Amazing that this trio of developers crafted such a landmark title. I bow to your triumvirate of talent. 

P.P.S : Incidentally, in case anyone is interested, my other Perfect 10 games are :

- Legend of Zelda : Ocarina of Time
- Resident Evil 4
- Batman : Arkham City
- Last of Us
- Telltale's The Walking Dead : Season 1

Very different from Orwell, but masterpieces for me in the revolution in video game design they brought to different elements of the industry.

game_name: Orwell: Keeping an Eye On You
review_text_raw:
I'll admit, I was skeptical, even with all the glowing reviews on Steam. However, bored with playing the same old games, I decided to give the game a try since it wasn't even 10$. As I started up the game, I asked myself - how this game could possibly keep me interested? It's a game where you're literally staring at a 'computer' screen in-game.. when you're already staring at a computer screen in real life. Not even 10 minutes in and I was hooked. I needed more information and I needed it NOW! I got really invested in the fictional characters stories, lives and background; why did she break up with him? How long were they dating? Why is 'X's relationship with her parents so strained? I looked through every single e-mail and chat message I could find. I listened to countless phone calls and actually cared what was said and listened intently. All the while snickering to myself because the fictional characters didn't know I was listening in on their conversations. 

This game proves that sometimes being innovative and creative pays off. The game was worth every last dollar. It's relatively short (6 hours) and  I played all the episodes straight through, but it still managed to keep me excited and interest throughout the whole game. I kept playing 'just 10 more minutes' to find new information. Although only 6 hours long, I felt like it's the perfect length. Any longer and I probably would have started getting annoyed (because I did want to find out the ending to the story). 

The only issues I had with the game was that it doesn't really explain how the 'upload information' works. It tells you very briefly what your job is - to upload information, but I didn't understand that I could literally choose what information to upload and what to withold. I thought I had to upload certain information to continue with the story - turns out that may not have necessarily been the case. I actually got an ending I didn't intend because even at the end of the game I wasn't really sure what I was supposed to be doing (how did I access information, not upload it but still continue with the story?). You would think 'upload information' would be an easy concept to understand and wouldn't really need a tutorial, but in my case I would have liked a proper 2-3 minute introduction to how Orwell 'works'. The fact that you can choose what you do and do not upload, and depending on that - there will be different concequences. 
The highlighting of relevant text kinda made the game too easy, but I do understand the necessity of the function. Any real-life program such as Orwell would probably have a similar feature that highlights relevant information. I felt like it made the game more realistic because occassionally while reading an on-going chat, I could quickly scan for relevant information that was highlighted - upload it - and then continue reading the conversation. 
I really idn't realize that my actions of uploading certain information would have concequences; I guess I thought the game was a lot more linear, not that I could actually influence what happened by what I did or did not upload. 

This was really unique, both in game-playstyle as well as story telling. I'll be playing it again, that's for sure.

game_name: Orwell: Keeping an Eye On You
review_text_raw:
Have you ever wondered what it’s like being the FBI that watches you all the time and snooping around your social media? 

WELL SAY NO MORE!! 

In this game you’ll experience how it feels like to spy on people and easily get information around. Whether it’s from your social media, desktop/laptop, phone, even your calls are recorded for further use as well. 

This game has taught me that every little information about us, private or not, can be misused and be used against us. CHOICES MATTER HERE which is why it has multiple endings, so that makes it more interesting. It's easy to learn but difficult to know what could trigger the other endings, but that's alright. 

The game is very politic and really shows you the two sides of society, it’s really up to you how you want this to end. I truly had fun playing this game, and highly recommend to play. 
- 9/10 Recommend

game_name: Orwell: Keeping an Eye On You
review_text_raw:
The premise for the game sounded interesting but I wasn't convinced on dropping money on it. Fortunately the free demo got me into the game, and that was all it took. I bought it immediately.

Although strictly speaking this is less of a game and more of an interactive novel, it is really, really good. My wife kept asking me to come to bed and I simply couldn't. I had to dig deeper into the mystery even knowing that in the end, I was the bad guy. I am the one spying on people and being part of a chilling government program.

Orwell is brilliant, and the developers and writers should be proud of themselves. I just finished downloading chapter 2 as I write this and I'm ready to get sucked back in.
